guide.summary: Notion documents OAuth 2.0 for connections where each customer user authorizes the app and picks pages to share. Access is bounded by the connection's Read content capability, with no OAuth scope strings; a read-only app should request only that capability.

findings.title: Public OAuth integration needed for any customer workspace
findings.detail: OAuth integrations use OAuth 2.0 with a client ID, client secret and redirect URI from the Developer portal. A selected-workspaces integration can be installed only in those workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace; installation scope cannot be changed after creation. Customer organizations require a public integration (Any workspace).

findings.title: Read content capability
findings.detail: Read content lets a connection read existing content; it is the only capability needed for reading page titles and content. Do not request Update content or Insert content. Access applies to pages the user shares through the page picker, including child pages of shared parents. Retrieve a page markdown requires read content or returns 403.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Open the Notion Developer portal, go to Build > Connections, and select Create new connection. Enter the connection name, development workspace and redirect URIs. For customer organizations choose the 'Any workspace' installation scope; it cannot be changed after creation and a selected-workspaces integration cannot serve other customer workspaces. In Capabilities choose only Read content (no Update or Insert content, no user information needed). Registration requires a Notion workspace member able to create connections.
steps.doneWhen: The connection exists with installation scope Any workspace, only Read content enabled, and the Configuration tab shows an OAuth client ID and client secret.

evidence.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection's installation scope — either **Any workspace** or **Or select 1

Select **Create new connection**. Enter the connection name, development workspace, and redirect URIs. Choose **Or select 1 or more workspaces**, select the workspaces, and choose the capabilities your app needs.
Open the **Configuration** tab to find your **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**. Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow.

steps.title: Prepare the redirect URI and server callback
steps.detail: Register each redirect URI exactly as your callback will receive it (for example https://example.com/auth/notion/callback). The agent can scaffold a server callback that reads the code, state and error query parameters (a cancelled consent returns ?error=access_denied&state=...). Generate a random state per request, store it server-side and verify it on return to prevent CSRF. Store client ID, client secret and tokens only in environment variables or a secret manager, never in source control or the browser.
steps.doneWhen: A callback route is deployed at the registered HTTPS redirect URI, verifies state, handles the error=access_denied case, and reads secrets only from the environment.

steps.title: Send a representative customer user through consent
steps.detail: A customer user (with full access to the pages to share) opens the authorization URL and approves, choosing pages in the page picker. Parent page selection includes child pages. Only the authorizing user can use that authorization, so each user must authorize individually. owner=user and response_type=code are always required; state is optional per docs but should be used here. The authorization URL is also shown in the Configuration tab. Run: curl -G 'https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize' --data-urlencode 'owner=user' --data-urlencode 'client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID' --data-urlencode 'redirect_uri=https://example.com/auth/notion/callback' --data-urlencode 'response_type=code' --data-urlencode 'state=YOUR_RANDOM_STATE' (normally opened in a browser).
steps.doneWhen: The browser lands on the redirect URI with a code query parameter and the same state value, and the authorizing user selected the intended pages.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: On the server, POST JSON to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth (CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET, base64). Body fields: grant_type=authorization_code, code (temporary code from the redirect), redirect_uri (required if sent in the authorization URL or if multiple URIs are registered). The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, owner and workspace_id. Store the full response per workspace in an encrypted store; never log it or expose it to the browser.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns access_token and refresh_token, which are stored encrypted and keyed by workspace_id and bot_id.
